system.name: Hierarchical Successor Representation (HSR)
system.one_liner: Successor representation built on temporally abstract options, giving policy-robust features whose NMF basis recovers room structure and transfers sample-efficiently.

content.variant_note: ten lettered panels: a derivation chain of formula nodes, three goal maps, then matrices, option maps, t-SNE plots and basis maps of one four-room environment
content.argues: Temporal abstraction turns diffusive, collapsed successor features into room-aware ones: eHSR with NMF recovers the four-room structure that RW-SR and eSR smear or collapse.
content.subject: Derivation chain of HSR plus four-room gridworld evidence: SR matrices, option maps, t-SNE plots and NMF or SVD basis maps.

lessons.what_to_learn: Pair a derivation chain of formula nodes (one colour per method, dashed versus dotted arrows for two decompositions) with result panels that reuse the same environment silhouette and the same method colours, so each symbol of the chain can be found as a picture.
lessons.suits: Representation-learning and RL theory papers whose claim is that one construction recovers structure that baselines blur, shown on a single small environment.

evidence: Schematic of the computational process underlying the construction of hierarchical successor representations
Classical SRs exhibit topological collapse: the predictive features of intra-compartment states are tightly clustered
HSR dynamics is piecewise-smooth, characterised by manifolds with effective intra-compartment dispersion

summary: The Hierarchical Successor Representation (HSR) builds the successor representation from temporally abstract options so that predictive features stay stable when policies change; NMF of the expected HSR (eHSR) then gives sparse, room-local features for transfer. Figure 1 packs ten lettered panels about one four-room gridworld. Panel a is a derivation chain of formula nodes: the random-walk SR (red) yields eigenvector options which, with the pretraining tasks G (b: three goal maps with S and G cells), give HSR and eHSR (blue), next to an SR and eSR baseline branch (orange); dashed and dotted arrows mark SVD and NMF bases. Panels c-f show SR matrices and option maps, g t-SNE plots where RW-SR and eSR collapse into tight clusters while eHSR spreads, and h-j basis maps.
summary_zh: HSR 用时间抽象的选项构造后继表示，并用 NMF 得到房间局部基。图 1 共十个面板：a 是从 RW-SR 到 eHSR 的推导链（虚线、点线分别表示 SVD、NMF），b 是三个四房间任务，其余用热图、t-SNE 和基向量图对比各方法。
notes: Prior label concept-schematic kept as primary; side-by-side-contrast added for the method comparisons in e-j and stage-pipeline for the arrow chain of panel a. The caption has slips (i called eigenvectors of eSR although the panel label and the text say eHSR; j says 'Same as j'). Arrow styles and labels in panel a are described as drawn; the orange hex is read off the preview, not the digest.
